scope: Actual dishwasher development sources only; no market-wide conclusion or independent-evaluation approval. Successful structure is distinct from semantic acceptance.

sources_reviewed.observation: The buyer wants easier dishwashing for their wife, whose legs hurt. The review mentions cleaning the rotating arms around one month of use, odor starting at an unspecified time, and return to handwashing after about three months total. It does not confirm joint disease, pain relief or recurrence, residue/cleaning-performance loss, failed odor treatment, disassembly, manual ignorance or incomplete cleaning.
Explicit convenience/drying/performance praise and surprise about adding rinse/detergent/salt coexist. A mixed experience should remain represented regardless of the five-star rating.
Low noise, good cleaning, saved housework time and friendly installation are explicitly praised.
Schedule/discussion problems are reported. The installer seeming unwilling is the customer's perception; the new normal summary retains that uncertainty.

Official shared DUE6 manual excerpts describe conditional odor guidance, not this customer's diagnosis/recovery. The residual-water guidance says more than 80 ml to 100 ml; it is conditional, not a new universal operating standard. Cleaning procedures reference separate maintenance chapters that are not included in this selected six-source input. Exact purchased SKU and purchase-time revision are unverified. The fishy-odor paragraph calls food trimethylamine alkaline and mentions acidic detergent, rather than establishing every detergent's acid/alkaline properties.

findings.assessment: The condition belongs to the buyer's wife, not necessarily the buyer. Sore legs do not establish joint disease or a measured recurrence of joint burden. A broader target cohort is allowed as an explicitly marked planning assumption, but no such persona assumption is listed. The concept cites only manuals while carrying a persona claim derived from the customer story; preserve the customer citation if using that experience.

findings.assessment: The known caveat says the cleaning/outcome sequence is unknown, but the before steps and scenes assert odor followed by treatment and persistent odor, disassembly, ignorance and failed cleaning. Those are not reported observations. Label new hypothetical before scenes in place and in assumptions, or limit them to the confirmed odor/handwashing experience. The total approximately three-month period is preserved in the description; no extra three-month period is added here.

Review 752651 expresses hoped-for convenience, odor, handwashing and disappointment, not an explicit positive use result; placing it in mixed while omitting negative is unsupported. Review 853593 explicitly combines praise with surprise, but its condensed positive-only summary drops the surprise and no mixed entry remains. Distinguish purchase expectation from actual satisfaction and preserve both stated sides of a mixed review.

Preserve the source's greater-than/condition context and verify the applicable model/document before actionable guidance. No new explicit unsafe disassembly command is found in after_steps, but the unsupported before-disassembly scene is already covered by CG-N-02. Keep the procedure/visualization proposal clearly provisional and require the actual referenced chapter.

It does not explicitly call cleaning an automatic product feature or declare the problem resolved, but separate what the customer did from what the manual advises and what remains unconfirmed.

improvements_vs_parent_normal: The same source snapshots, parent brief and revision increment are preserved while the concept shifts to an app/web checklist and recorded customer-support handoff.
The joint-disease target and joint-burden recurrence claim disappear; target_user is now customers affected by odor or returning to handwashing.
The concept now cites the customer review as well as the two official excerpts.
The residual-water quantity is described as exceeding 80–100 ml in comparison, preserving the greater-than condition better than the normal concept.
The 853593 summary now retains the surprise about rinse/detergent/salt in its text, although its positive-only placement still misses the mixed experience.
No echoed guidance, output truncation, unreported cleaning-performance loss or explicit diagnosis/recovery promise appears.

findings.assessment: The original says the buyer’s wife has sore legs. This is still assigned to the customer/buyer. The caveat correctly says the cleaning/odor chronology and outcome are unknown, but the description still implies failed treatment. Removing the medical persona elsewhere does not repair this observation.

These steps/scenes infer manual use, confusion, odor→cleaning→persistent/recurrent odor and prior support contact, none of which the review establishes. Listing an all-methods-failed assumption does not establish these other observations. comparison_limits correctly preserves uncertainty, but remaining_burden nonetheless narrows the experience to unverified failure/nonexecution explanations. This is not a renewed manual-exists→resolved claim; it is an unsupported manual-failure/history claim. Mark proposed before scenes as hypothetical in place, and leave actual cause/action/outcome unknown.

The one-month reference concerns use around the reported cleaning mention. The review reports about three months total before handwashing. Automatically handing support a one-month total use period is a new false fact. A future flow should ask the customer to confirm duration/action history; for this reported case preserve approximately three months and distinguish the roughly one-month maintenance reference.

findings.assessment: These are condition-specific guidance branches, not three mandatory actions for every odor case. The cited drain procedure requires excess residual water, powering on, then holding the power button three seconds to select cancellation; the short comparison omits that full sequence. The quantities are present in the source, not invented, but the applicable SKU/current version and conditions remain unverified. Do not demand detergent purchase/prewash/draining before every support handoff, or synthesize cleaning steps from page-49 references to another chapter. Keep a reference/confirmation path and allow unresolved or inapplicable cases to be shared without claiming a confirmed cause or guaranteed solution.
